title: Probability
ks3: Probability: the probability scale, single events, expected results and combined events
intro: How likely is it? Practise probability words, the probability scale, working out probabilities as fractions and decimals, and expected results.
description: Free KS3 Maths probability questions with answers: certain, likely and impossible, the 0 to 1 scale, probability of single events, expected outcomes and two events. Marked instantly, for Year 7, 8 and 9 (ages 9 to 14).

questions.q: Which word best describes the chance that the Sun will rise tomorrow?
questions.hint: Has there ever been a day when it didn't?
questions.explain: The Sun rises every day, so it is certain. Certain has a probability of 1.

questions.q: Rolling a 7 on an ordinary dice numbered 1 to 6 is…
questions.hint: Which numbers are on the dice?
questions.explain: There is no 7 on the dice, so it can't happen: it is impossible, with a probability of 0.

questions.q: You flip a fair coin. The chance of getting heads is…
questions.hint: There are two sides, and each is equally likely.
questions.explain: Heads and tails are equally likely, so heads has an even chance: a probability of {1/2}.

questions.q: On the probability scale from 0 to 1, where is "impossible"?
questions.hint: The scale starts with things that can never happen.
questions.explain: Impossible is 0, even chance is {1/2} and certain is 1. A probability can never be more than 1.

questions.q: A bag has 9 red sweets and 1 green sweet. You take one without looking. Getting a red sweet is…
questions.hint: There are lots of red ones, but is there any other colour?
questions.explain: Most of the sweets are red, so red is likely. It is not certain, because you could pick the green one.

questions.q: The spinner is spun once. What is the probability that it lands on red?
questions.hint: Count the red sections and all the sections. Probability = red sections ÷ all sections.
questions.explain: 2 of the 4 equal sections are red, so the probability is {2/4} = {1/2}.

questions.q: This spinner is spun once. What is the probability that it lands on blue?
questions.hint: How many sections are blue? How many sections are there altogether?
questions.explain: 2 of the 8 equal sections are blue, so the probability is {2/8} = {1/4}.

questions.q: A fair dice is rolled. What is the probability of rolling a number greater than 4?
questions.hint: Which numbers on a dice are greater than 4?
questions.explain: 5 and 6 are greater than 4: 2 out of 6 numbers. The probability is {2/6} = {1/3}.

questions.q: A bag has 3 red, 5 blue and 2 green counters. One counter is taken at random. What is the probability that it is blue?
questions.hint: How many counters are there altogether?
questions.explain: There are 3 + 5 + 2 = 10 counters and 5 are blue, so the probability is {5/10} = {1/2}.

questions.q: The same bag has 3 red, 5 blue and 2 green counters. What is the probability that the counter taken is not green?
questions.hint: How many counters are not green?
questions.explain: 8 of the 10 counters are not green, so the probability is {8/10} = {4/5}. (Or: 1 − {2/10} = {8/10}.)

questions.q: The probability that it will rain tomorrow is 0.3. What is the probability that it will not rain?
questions.hint: It either rains or it doesn't, so the two probabilities add up to 1.

questions.q: The spinner is spun once. What is the probability that it lands on blue?
questions.hint: Count the blue sections and all the sections.
questions.explain: 3 of the 5 equal sections are blue, so the probability is {3/5}.

questions.q: A fair dice numbered 1 to 6 is rolled. What is the probability of rolling a 4?
questions.hint: How many 4s are there? How many numbers altogether?
questions.explain: There is one 4 out of 6 equally likely numbers, so the probability is {1/6}.

questions.q: The letters of the word BANANA are put on cards. One card is picked at random. What is the probability that it shows the letter A?
questions.hint: Count every letter, including the ones that repeat.
questions.explain: BANANA has 6 letters and 3 of them are A, so the probability is {3/6} = {1/2}.

questions.q: A jar has 24 sweets. The probability of picking a red sweet is {3/8}. How many red sweets are in the jar?
questions.hint: Find {1/8} of 24 first.
questions.explain: {1/8} of 24 is 24 ÷ 8 = 3, so {3/8} of 24 is 3 × 3 = 9 red sweets.

questions.q: A bag has only red, blue and green counters. The probability of red is 0.25 and the probability of blue is 0.4. What is the probability of green?
questions.hint: All the probabilities must add up to 1.
questions.explain: 0.25 + 0.4 = 0.65, so the probability of green is 1 − 0.65 = 0.35.

questions.q: A fair coin has landed on heads 5 times in a row. What is the probability of heads on the next flip?
questions.hint: Does the coin remember what happened before?
questions.explain: Each flip is independent: the coin has no memory. The probability of heads is still {1/2}.

questions.q: A fair coin is flipped 200 times. About how many heads would you expect?
questions.hint: The probability of heads is {1/2}.
questions.explain: {1/2} × 200 = 100 heads. The real result will probably be close to 100, but not exactly.

questions.q: The probability that a spinner lands on 5 is 0.15. It is spun 60 times. How many times would you expect it to land on 5?
questions.hint: Expected number = probability × number of spins.

questions.q: A fair dice is rolled 60 times. About how many times would you expect to roll a 6?
questions.hint: The probability of a 6 is {1/6}.

questions.q: Ella drops a piece of toast 50 times. It lands butter side down 30 times. Estimate the probability that it lands butter side down. Give your answer as a decimal.
questions.hint: Estimated probability = number of times it happened ÷ number of tries.
questions.explain: 30 ÷ 50 = {3/5} = 0.6. This is called the relative frequency.

questions.q: You flip a coin and roll a dice numbered 1 to 6. How many different outcomes are possible (like heads and 3)?
questions.hint: List them, or multiply the number of outcomes for each.
questions.explain: The coin has 2 outcomes and the dice has 6, so there are 2 × 6 = 12 outcomes: H1, H2, …, H6, T1, …, T6.

questions.q: Two fair coins are flipped. What is the probability of getting two heads?
questions.hint: List all the outcomes: HH, HT, …
questions.explain: The outcomes are HH, HT, TH and TT. Only 1 of the 4 is two heads, so the probability is {1/4}.

questions.q: The school lunch menu has 3 main courses and 2 puddings. How many different meals of one main and one pudding can you choose?
questions.hint: List them, or multiply the number of choices for each part.
questions.explain: Each of the 3 mains can go with either of the 2 puddings: 3 × 2 = 6 meals.

questions.q: Two fair dice are rolled and the scores are added. What is the probability that the total is 7?
questions.hint: Draw a 6 by 6 grid of all the outcomes. How many give a total of 7?
questions.explain: There are 6 × 6 = 36 outcomes. Six give 7: 1+6, 2+5, 3+4, 4+3, 5+2, 6+1. The probability is {6/36} = {1/6}.

questions.q: A fair spinner numbered 1, 2 and 3 is spun and a fair coin is flipped. What is the probability of getting tails and an odd number?
questions.hint: List every outcome, like H1, H2, …
questions.explain: The 6 outcomes are H1, H2, H3, T1, T2, T3. Tails and odd is T1 or T3: 2 out of 6, so the probability is {2/6} = {1/3}.
